DataPipe saves **one CSV file per participant**. This document reads all of
them and finds the average rating on each measure for GPT vs. PNAS summaries.

## Load packages

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)  # wrangling + ggplot2
library(here)       # file paths relative to the project folder
library(lme4)       # mixed models
library(lmerTest)   # p-values for lmer
library(jsonlite)   # parse JSON-looking response strings, if any
```

## Read in all the data files

The pilot files are in `markowitz2024 data/raw/pilot A/`, one folder up from
this project. As more participant data comes into my Google Drive DataPipe folder, I will put their files in this same folder and they will all be read in.

```{r}
files <- list.files(here("..", "markowitz2024 data", "raw", "pilot A"),
                    pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
files
```

`read_csv()` can read a whole list of files and stack them into one table.

```{r}
all_data <- read_csv(files, show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Keep only the rating trials

The `response` column also holds consent, demographic, and survey answers, so
R reads it as text. Rating trials are the only rows with a `measure_block`
(the other rows say `"null"`). Once we keep only those rows, we turn
`response` back into numbers with `as.numeric()`.

```{r}
ratings <- all_data |>
  filter(measure_block != "null") |>
  mutate(response = as.numeric(response)) |>
  select(subject_id, stimulus_id, version, measure_block, measure, response)

ratings
```

## Average rating for each measure

```{r}
measure_means <- ratings |>
  group_by(measure_block, measure, version) |>
  summarise(mean_rating = mean(response), .groups = "drop")

measure_means
```

```{r}
ggplot(measure_means, aes(x = mean_rating, y = measure, fill = version)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(x = "Mean rating (1-7)", y = "Measure", fill = "Summary version")
```
